rationale: D7 DEPTH — THE `importedName` CLAIM (Lead arbiter, charter §18.19), pinned in both directions. A BARE name the file imports from a stdlib-rooted specifier names a binding that occupies THIS FILE's scope, so the honest row is a CLAIM verified from the run's own import evidence (the analyzer's moduleImportBindings map: name -> specifier, certified from the file's own `from X import name` syntax), counted in the binding family (`bindOK`, verifiedBy importEvidence) and NEVER resolved. The POSITIVE row is `from tempfile import mkstemp` + `mkstemp()`: the claim carries {specifier: tempfile, name: mkstemp}, and `tempfile` is a `python-stdlib` vocabulary root (script/m14/citations.ts). The NEGATIVE rows are the principled restriction, not arbitrary: (a) a bare name the file never imports (orphan_use) carries NO claim — there is no evidence to verify it, so the arbiter would REFUTE it; (b) a RELATIVE specifier (`.helpers`) is this project BY THE GRAMMAR, so no citation; (c) a THIRD-PARTY root (requests) can be the project's own code in its own checkout (the kotlinx precedent), so it stays a NAMED class in the D7 ledger until a project-module test exists — it is not marked and not laundered. The gate-side refutation controls (target != name, name not name-shaped, name not imported, specifier not imported, no evidence) live in the Lead's selfTest battery; this fixture pins the LANE's emission side.
